//1: subagent-driven-development SKILL.md, MIT (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent, adapted for
//2: doomalay v0.42). Executes an implementation plan with a fresh implementer per
//3: task, a two-verdict task review (spec compliance + code quality), a 5-round
//4: capped fix loop (rounds 1-3 resume the implementer, rounds 4-5 escalate to a
//5: fresh implementer on a more capable model), a workspace-persisted LEDGER that
//6: survives compaction, Rulings-not-stalls conflict resolution, and a final
//7: whole-branch review. Pass the implementation plan as the prompt.
//8: FIX LOOP NOTE: the review->fix->re-review cycle is expressed as the
//9: task_review -> fix_round -> re_review stage chain; the orchestrator's
//10: max_rounds retry is the outer harness. Per-task fix rounds are capped at 5
//11: in the instructions (the breaker: at the cap, every open finding is adjudicated
//12: into the ledger as Ruling/parked, never silently dropped).
task: <FILL ME IN: implementation plan to execute task-by-task>

stages.name: parse_plan
stages.instructions: Parse the implementation plan. Output JSON {"plan_path": str, "spec_path": str, "global_constraints": [str], "tasks": [{"n": int, "name": str, "files": [str], "interfaces_consumes": [str], "interfaces_produces": [str], "test_command": str}]}. Copy global constraints VERBATIM from the plan's Global Constraints section. Carry each task's Interfaces blocks exactly - implementers see only their own task. If the plan names a Spec, carry its path (the spec is the binding authority the plan argues from; conflicts resolve against it). Return ONLY a single JSON object.

stages.name: preflight
stages.instructions: Pre-flight conflict scan, superpowers SDD style - bulleted findings only. One row for every pair of tasks that share a file or an interface: the two tasks, what one produces against what the other consumes, and whether they agree. One row for every task: does its own text agree with itself (tests it specifies vs code it specifies, files it creates vs files it later touches)? Tasks that share nothing get no row; if NO tasks share anything, emit the single bullet 'Pre-flight: no shared interfaces'. Also flag anything the plan explicitly mandates that a review rubric would call a defect (a test that asserts nothing, verbatim duplication of a logic block). The scan's output is a table, not a verdict - 'the scan is clean' without rows is not a scan you ran.

stages.name: implement
stages.instructions: You are a fresh implementer sub-agent for ONE plan task (the one assigned to you) - never the session's history. Follow the implementer contract: (1) implement EXACTLY what the task specifies under TDD - write the failing test, watch it fail for the right reason, minimal code to pass, run the tests; (2) commit as the task's commit steps say; (3) self-review your diff with fresh eyes (completeness, quality, discipline, test hygiene) and fix what you find BEFORE reporting; (4) never spawn sub-agents of your own - not helpers, never a reviewer: review arrives from the controller after your report. If the task requires architectural decisions with multiple valid approaches, or you cannot find clarity after genuinely trying, report status BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT with what you are stuck on, what you tried, and the help you need - bad work is worse than no work. Carry any pre-flight ruling that touches your task (from the preflight input) - it is the controller's resolution of ambiguity in the brief. End your output with the short status contract: 'Status: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT', the commits created, a one-line test summary, and concerns if any. Write the full detailed report as a '## Report' section above the status block (what you implemented, tests run + results, TDD evidence RED->GREEN, files changed, self-review findings).

stages.name: task_review
stages.instructions: You are a task reviewer - two verdicts, this is a task-scoped gate (the broad whole-branch review happens at the end). Review the implementer's output for YOUR task. Part 1 SPEC COMPLIANCE: Missing (requirements skipped or claimed without implementing), Extra (features that were not requested, over-engineering), Misunderstood (right feature, wrong problem). If a requirement cannot be verified from the implementation alone, report it as a 'CANNOT VERIFY FROM DIFF' item. Part 2 CODE QUALITY: clean separation of concerns, proper error handling, DRY without premature abstraction, edge cases, tests verify real behavior not mocks, file responsibilities. Treat the implementer's report as UNVERIFIED CLAIMS - verify against what was actually produced; a stated rationale never downgrades a finding's severity. CALIBRATION: Important means this task cannot be trusted until fixed (incorrect/fragile behavior, missed requirement, maintainability damage - verbatim duplicated logic, swallowed errors, tests that assert nothing); 'coverage could be broader' and polish are Minor. If the plan explicitly mandates something this rubric calls a defect, report it as Important labeled plan-mandated. Output format: '### Task <N> Review' -> 'Spec: PASS | FAIL: <what>' + any CANNOT-VERIFY items -> '### Strengths' -> '### Issues' grouped Critical / Important / Minor (each: what is wrong, why it matters, how to fix) -> 'Task quality: Approved | Needs fixes'.

stages.name: fix_round
stages.instructions: Fix round for YOUR task's review findings. RULES OF THE LOOP (superpowers fix loop): a fix round triggers on spec FAIL, any Critical/Important finding, or a confirmed CANNOT-VERIFY gap. Minor findings NEVER enter the loop - defer them to the ledger. A finding that conflicts with plan text is the controller's to rule on (spec is the binding authority); if you must deviate from the plan to fix a finding, say so in a 'Ruling:' line. Fix ALL open Critical/Important findings in ONE pass: write the covering test first (watch it fail), fix, re-run the covering tests (a one-line fix does not need the whole suite), and append a fix report (what changed, covering tests, command, output). Rounds 1-3: you are the original implementer resumed - your context is intact. Rounds 4-5: fresh implementer on a more capable model - say so and read the prior report carefully. THE CAP: 5 rounds maximum. At the cap, the breaker trips: do NOT attempt round 6. Instead adjudicate each remaining open finding: parked (reviewer wrong or contestable - 'Parked: <finding> - Ruling: <why the code stands>'), parked-deferred (real but nothing builds on it), or load-bearing (rule on the smallest change that unblocks dependents, as 'Ruling: <what you decided and why>'). Every adjudication is a ledger entry - a silent discard is forbidden.

stages.name: re_review
stages.instructions: Scoped re-review of YOUR task's fix round - the full review already happened; your scope is the findings list and the fix. Verdict EVERY finding from the task_review input: ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED (with where). Check the fix report names the covering tests and shows their output - treat the report as unverified claims and verify what you can. Flag NEW breakage the fix itself introduced (only in the fixed code). Out-of-scope observations go under 'Out-of-Scope Observations' - they do not block and do not extend the loop. Never suggest re-running whole suites the implementer already ran. Output: per-finding verdicts, new-breakage list, out-of-scope list, and a round verdict line 'Verdict: all findings addressed | <K> open'.

stages.name: ledger
stages.instructions: Write the SDD LEDGER - the artifact that survives compaction - as a markdown document titled '# SDD ledger - plan: <plan_path>' (this content is also written to the file '.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/progress.md' in the session workspace, and read back as the first input on any resumed run). One line per task in order: 'Task <N>: complete (review clean)' or 'Task <N>: complete (<K> parked)' or 'Task <N>: INCOMPLETE - <status>'. Every fix round: 'Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> open; <one-liners>)'. Every deferred minor: 'Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>'. Then a '## Rulings I made' section listing EVERY Ruling/Parked line from preflight, fix rounds, and breakers, in order, each with what it costs if wrong - the list is exhaustive: a ruling that dies with the workspace was a decision made in secret. Then '## Deferred minors' (every minor, one line each). The ledger is the recovery map: after compaction, trust it and git log over recollection - tasks with a complete line are DONE, never re-dispatched.

stages.name: final_review
stages.instructions: Final whole-branch code review (the superpowers most-capable-model seat): review the ENTIRE plan execution as one branch. The spec is a vision document - for behavior it is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this software would expect; grade findings by EFFECT on that person, not by whether the spec names the trigger. Check plan alignment (all planned functionality present; deviations justified), code quality across task boundaries (integration seams, error handling, DRY), architecture soundness, and test quality (real behavior, edge cases from the Review Focus). Triage the ledger's deferred minors and parked rulings: which MUST be fixed before merge, which stand. Before the verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside as outside the plan ('Declined to judge') - one line each with the reason; nothing set aside is dropped silently. Output: '### Strengths' -> '### Issues' Critical/Important/Minor with file references -> '### Deferred-minor triage' -> '### Assessment: Ready to proceed | With fixes'.

stages.name: verify
stages.instructions: Output JSON {"pass": bool, "reason": str}. pass=false if ANY of: a task was completed without review verdicts (both spec compliance AND quality); the fix loop exceeded 5 rounds or an open Critical/Important finding is neither fixed nor parked-with-ruling; the ledger is missing Rulings, deferred minors, or per-task completion lines; a silent discard (finding vanished with no fix and no ruling); the final whole-branch review or its deferred-minor triage is missing. Otherwise pass=true.

llm_judges: Does every task carry BOTH review verdicts (spec compliance and code quality) before being marked complete?
Is every un-fixed finding either parked with a recorded ruling or listed as load-bearing, with none silently dropped?
